title: BEVControl: Accurately Controlling Street-view Elements with Multi-perspective Consistency via BEV Sketch Layout
control_family: layout, box, map or BEV conditioning

output_modality.value: other: multi-view street-view images (six camera perspectives per BEV layout, single frame rather than video)

control_signal.value: Editable BEV sketch (160 x 160 m around ego) with five channels: road line, box centre, text label and heading of foreground objects; plus a text prompt.

control_mechanism.value: Sketch is projected to each camera view; a Controller embeds foreground boxes and background road hints via self-attention, a Coordinator adds cross-view-cross-element attention; text via cross-attention. Only newly added layers are trained.

base_model.value: Latent-diffusion style UNet (LDM) fine-tuned from a pretrained diffusion model [14]; original diffusion layers frozen; CLIP used for label embedding.

datasets.value: nuScenes; six cameras per frame; 600 validation frames sampled as the validation subset for evaluation.

metrics.value: FID for realism and diversity, CLIP score for cross-view consistency, BEVFormer mAP/NDS/mAOE and CVT mIoU for foreground and background control, downstream NDS.

controllability_evidence.value: Detection and segmentation on generated images versus the input layout; foreground segmentation mIoU rises from 5.89 (BEVGen) to 26.80; training on generated data gives on average 1.29 NDS improvement.

closed_loop.value: No; per-frame image generation from a layout, no interactive rollout with a driving policy described in the packet.

stated_limitations.value: Future work: control further visual elements such as lighting and weather, which are not controlled now, and transfer the idea to more general scenes.

notes: Image generator, not a temporal world model. Which pretrained model [14] is used is not named in the packet text; the packet only cites it by number.
